utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Witness. Mr. Robinson, you have someone to introduce.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I do. Thank you very much, Mr. President. Our legal intern Hae Jin Choo is joining us for this first session this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I want to move ahead now and ask you some questions about events in Zvornik which you've talked about in your statement and before, and the first one is described in paragraph 93 and 94 of your statement and that is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think the witness can't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you hear me now, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I didn't receive translation earlier, I would kindly ask you to repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I will. I'm going to ask you now, moving ahead, about some incidents which occurred in Zvornik in the May-June period and earlier that you've talked about before, and the first one is in 93 and 94 of your statement and that relates to Celopek. Was there a detention facility during that time in Celopek that you heard about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a citizen of Zvornik, I did hear that that existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. Which people were detained in Celopek, can you describe what you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that Muslims were being detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And which village were these Muslims from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think it was Divic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And describe what type of conditions you heard as a citizen of Zvornik at the time these men were detained in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any details. I just heard that they were detained at the cultural centre in Celopek.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Which unit, force, group, who guarded these men from Divic in Celopek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me just try to remind you from your statement and if you don't know, you can explain. You stated that, in para 94: "As far as I know, Zuca's unit controlled the jail in Celopek and they were very abusive in their behaviour." One sentence later: "Terrible stories were being told in town about what Zuca and his men did in Celopek." So can you tell me what some of those terrible stories were that you heard about Zuca's men in Celopek?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I'm going to object to this. I know that hearsay is allowed here at the Tribunal, but now we're just repeating rumours, and unless there's more foundation for what the source of the information was that the witness is going to repeat in court, I think it should be excluded. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think Mr. Nicholls is trying to refresh his memory, having heard his first answer, I think it's fair enough. We'll see how the witness is able to answer the question. Did you complete your question, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any direct knowledge. What I stated is what is contained in my statement. That is what I read in the newspapers about their trial and that is what I heard from some unofficial sources too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what were those unofficial sources?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was being talked about. These people were on trial, the newspapers wrote about it, it was in the media, there was talk in town that there were paramilitaries there - I'm not sure which ones - that they controlled that unit. But I don't know any further details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to now ask you about an event that you may know more about, and that is Djulici and Karakaj technical school, moving on in your statement. Now, Djulici, was that a Serb or an ethnic neighbourhood or area -- Serb or Muslim I mean to say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Djulici was a purely Muslim town and there were a few other Muslim villages that gravitated towards that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, in June 1992, approximately how many Muslim residents were in the Djulici area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly but I think that about 3- or 4.000 Muslims gravitated in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Why did they gravitate to that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I'm not sure what gravitated means. They are geographically linked up, these villages around Djulici, that is what it means as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, in June in Zvornik municipality, the area of Kozluk, the Muslim area of Kozluk, how big was that area in terms of towns or villages in the Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Kozluk is a small town that had a population of about 3- to 4.000 and perhaps 85 per cent were Muslim, but there were also a few villages there, Skocic, Gornji Sepak, that are 4 or 5 kilometres away from Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In your statement you said it was the second-biggest city this area comprised after Zvornik, is that right, second-biggest city after Zvornik in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the second-largest settlement. You couldn't really call it a city. It's a very small town.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And I'm not, for time, going to go into the entire chronology, that in July were there Muslims -- by the end of July was the population of Kozluk -- the Muslim population of Kozluk still residing in Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the majority of them were still residing in Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, Witness, just -- I really do not want to spend a lot of time on this. In your statement at paragraph 107 you say that: "In June 1992, however, the situation changed and the Muslims at Kozluk moved." Not a few Muslims, not a small percentage, but that "the Muslims of Kozluk moved." Is that right or not right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I wasn't paying attention to the date that you mentioned, that was July 1992. From the beginning of the hostilities they remained living there until a date in June when they were removed from Kozluk and they went to Hungary.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now I want to move on again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We should probably go into private session for a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, can you tell me -- you've talked quite a lot about these volunteers, paramilitaries. Tell me as briefly as you can about how they came to be arrested.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the time I was in the commercial sector. I don't know any details. All I know is that a special MUP unit came, led by Milenko Karisik, together with some supporting personnel from another unit. Before that, the intelligence service gathered information about their places of residence and just one morning all of them were arrested and taken to the prison in Zvornik. What surprised all of us, it was really a shock to all of us who were familiar with the developments in Zvornik, was that among those arrested was Marko Pavlovic. I even think that Grujic, the president of the municipality, himself was surprised and that he called some services to try and intervene through some MUP channels, but he was told to leave it and to allow the judiciary and other organs to do their job regardless of everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And who was it who told him to leave it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean particularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, you said that. "... Grujic, the president of the municipality, himself was surprised and that he called some services to try and intervene through some MUP channels, but he was told to leave it ..." That's what I mean, who was it who told him to leave it, in your words, and not intervene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Karisik, he was in charge of that operation, Milenko Karisik. I think he was an officer in the police of Republika Srpska, but I don't know which rank he held.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you recall an event which precipitated the arrest of the paramilitaries in which they detained a minister of the government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was talk in town that Mr. Ostojic, who was the minister for information, was arrested at that time as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just to be clear, arrested by the paramilitaries not by the special police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, by the paramilitary troops stationed at Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when you said earlier in your answer about the judiciary and other organs to do their jobs, when the -- was that done, do you know what happened to these men after they were arrested, what their punishments were, how long they were held, that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how this process went along. I know that another proceedings were conducted in Sabac. Zuca's brother was convicted there and I think he committed suicide in prison.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters didn't hear the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know at all whether these proceedings have been brought to a completion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, other than some of the leaders, the - I'll call them - rank-and-file members of these paramilitaries, do you know what happened to them, whether they were tried, sentenced; or whether they ended up returning to regular units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not all members of the paramilitary were arrested on that occasion. Only their leaders were arrested and their units were disbanded. Some of the men were expelled back to Serbia, and I remember that there was a list of people who were banned from crossing the border to Republika Srpska. That's as far as the leaders are concerned. Among ordinary members that contained and consisted of local people as well, they were returned to regular units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to quickly bring up 22840 -- or, excuse me, P01478. And the English, please, as well as the Serbian transcript. We can go to page 1 first. I actually meant the cover --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this is Mladic's diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. -- we can go, please, straight to page 246 of the English and 244 of the Serbian. Mr. Witness, this is the handwritten notebook kept by Ratko Mladic during the period that included June 1992, and I want to show you some pages from a meeting held in Zvornik on the 30th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if I could have the -- I think it's easier to use the typed Serbian rather than the handwritten. There should be two versions in e-court. And again in the English it should be page 246 and one page -- sorry. English page 246 and in the B/C/S 244.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Witness, while this is coming up, can I ask you if you have been shown this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time that I see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. Back one page in the B/C/S to 243.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Witness, take a look first -- if you can, you can read along in the version you understand. I'd like you to look at the people who attended this meeting in Zvornik on the 30th of June in the afternoon. General Mladic has entitled it: "Meeting with representatives of Zvornik municipality." And he lists the people present including himself and President, at that time, Karadzic. Number 3 is the president of the Bratunac municipality, Ljubisav Simic. Did you know Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Tell me how you knew him, whether it was a friend, whether it was through SDS, how -- just to how -- what your relationship was with him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, we are in -- just a second, we are in public session. Is it okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, you're correct, Your Honour. Thank you. We're probably better to -- I don't know what his answer will be so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we go back to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And, Witness, do you see as well at the top number 18, that Marko Pavlovic --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: -- and Branko Grujic attended? I'm just informing -- because you haven't seen this before, I'm showing you who was there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Now, most of these persons speak, but I'm going to concentrate on those mainly from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we skip ahead two pages to page 249 of the English and two more pages in the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what I want you to concentrate on is what Branko Grujic, listed here as representative of the interim government, reports to the president and to Mladic at this meeting. "We have 32.000 Serbs. "We have successfully implemented the President's decision to settle Divic and Kozluk with our children," it continues on the next page. Now, Divic I think you said is the area where the residents were kept, you heard, in Celopek under terrible conditions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the majority of Divic residents were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. If we continue --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We need to go to the next pages, please, in both.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Here Grujic speaks about Marko Pavlovic. "Marko Pavlovic accomplished much until the formation of the brigade." And then Mr. Grujic describes problems with the paramilitaries, Zuca's group, et cetera. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to show you a couple more entries and then I'll ask you my question about these comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could go over to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, here, very simply, we see that the next speaker who General Mladic is taking notes of is Marko Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can we continue to the next page where we don't need to go through this part of the background he gives.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And here at the top Pavlovic also talks about what happened with the voluntary -- with the volunteer formations. And he says they: "... enjoyed exceptional success, they were led by Arkan and Seselj. "Arkan's withdrew orderly, but some that stayed broke free of his control."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can we go over to the next page in both.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And here we see Pavlovic giving a briefing of what's happened, the brigade's been formed, the problematic areas of Medjedja and Sapna, entering the village of Kovacevici, where people fled because of cowardice, conflicts, morale is not as good as it should be. And at the bottom: "We were most active in evicting the Muslims ..." We can go to the next page where it continues. "We brought peace to Sepak, Divic, and Kozluk. Some of them wanted to move out, while we demanded it. "We had to evict some of the people also for the sake of our 'heros' who fled from Kovacevici." And now I'll skip ahead to page 258 of the English, please. And I believe 256 of the B/C/S. Now, following these reports from the Zvornik head of the provisional government, the Zvornik TO commander, Mr. Simic, president of Bratunac municipality, reports. And he speaks of his municipality and says: "Until 1968 it had a Serbian majority population. Since then they moved to Serbia. So according to the last census it was 64:36 in favour of the Muslims. "In Bratunac municipality we now have two Muslims. "We used to have paramilitary formations, today we have a clear situation ..." And then he goes on to other matters. Now, I'd like your comment, Witness, on the way these two municipality leaders and the TO commander from your municipality have lauded and described the removal of the Muslims -- populations and described that as bringing peace at the same time that they're complaining about the actions of the paramilitaries who have broken free from control. Was that what was in fact going on in Zvornik and Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have no comment on this. I think that an expert of some sort would be better placed to comment on this than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I ask because you were present, Witness. We've talked about the removal of the Muslims from Divic. We've talked about the removal of the Muslims from Djulici. We've talked about the removal of the Muslims from Kozluk. This has been reported in a positive light. Was that -- you were -- you knew these people. Was that the way it was considered at that time in Zvornik and, to your knowledge, Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this, you are equating Divic, Djulici, and Kozluk, which in my view is like the difference between day and night. Kozluk was evacuated under completely different circumstances as opposed to those in Divic and Djulici. The war was on and I myself also wasn't very happy about going to work through Djulici where I was stopped once and my weapons were seized from me. And also, alternatively, the Muslims didn't like having Serbs around when the war is going on. If you have your family, your children, around you and you feel threatened, there's no other way to act. I would have liked to have them at least 100 kilometres away from me and I think that they had the same wish when it refers to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What happened to the mosques in Zvornik after the take-over in early April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This enormous hatred that was increasing over the years ended in the destruction of all churches and mosques in every village virtually. That was one of the effects of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. So just does that mean that the mosques in Zvornik were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you know by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information, but they were not destroyed in war operations. They were destroyed later when Zvornik became 100 per cent Serb when there were no Muslims left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. July 19 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we go into private session for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, now we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. At the beginning to identify the witness because I used the statement, which has not been admitted, so I think it would be best just for the record to now, if Your Honours think it's required, shall I show the pseudonym sheet? Because the statement has not been admitted which he identified his name on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we admit the first page, cover page?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's perfectly fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be done. That will be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3158, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That concludes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We have about 15 more minutes to have a break, but if it is convenient we may take a break now. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. We need to bring our case manager in also, so if we could do that, that would be good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we go into private session briefly. There's some matter to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we'll break for 20 minutes and resume at 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. Good morning, Your Excellencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Witness. Good morning to all. First of all I would like to thank you, Mr. Witness, for having been so kind as to communicate with the Defence by way of a videolink. I hope that that will help us be as specific as possible and expeditious as possible. I have to ask you -- I have to tell you that I asked for a lot more time for cross-examination. I was given a lot less. So I'll try to be as specific as possible so I need answers that are as brief as possible, so I kindly ask you to provide answers that are as brief as possible and please let us wait for the interpretation. You didn't have that problem with Mr. Nicholls but there is going to be a problem with me if we overlap. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that we had not known each other before you came to this position, and it wasn't as soon as you were appointed but considerably later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that no one from the SDS headquarters interfered in local personnel lists and that you were a candidate at local level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: During the old communist system, was it customary that certain positions in government would be allocated to the Serb people and the Muslim people and the Croat people where the said people were a majority, for instance, Croats? And were you in a position that had been allocated to the Serb people and the party that won the votes of the Serb people nominates such a candidate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, reciprocity was always observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the recommendation that the SDS gave to local personnel commissions was that ministries should be given proposals containing the names of two or three individuals, and then the minister would have the freedom to select one particular candidate among them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was on a list that contained three candidates and I was appointed by Minister Alija Delimustafic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. We're not going to go into any detail. So it wasn't the SDS that appointed you. The SDS proposed you as a candidate and the minister appointed you; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the war and during this brief period of the war, is it correct that you did not communicate with the SDS but only with your ministry according to the lines involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it then also correct that you did not take part in SDS policy-making, not even at local level let alone central level or higher levels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that many people or some people would try to sound more important by saying that they were communicating with ministers, the headquarters of the party, security services in Serbia, and so on; were there things like that going on, that people would try to represent themselves falsely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like us to clarify a particular situation in relation to Crisis Staffs. Do you remember that at the level of the SDS of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina there was an ad hoc Crisis Staff that had been established at the time of the roadblocks on the 1st of March? It was headed by the president of the Executive Board, Rajko Dukic. Is that the Crisis Staff that you referred to in some of your statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see or come to realise that this Crisis Staff ever functioned after the 3rd of March, after the roadblocks were put up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it did not function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, let's go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With the permission of the participants, I am going to put something to you, something that you said somewhere; and then if there is any misunderstanding we are going to move into private session so that we can have this sorted out. Did you testify before to the effect that you were not in charge of communications between yourself and the headquarters of the party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but I would like to get cite references where possible. I just tell Mr. Karadzic as he moves along in general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We go back to private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, therefore, that neither you nor Mr. Grujic had any contacts or channels of communication with the central organs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now yet again can we move into private session briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, did Mr. Alic work in Zvornik on linking up active-duty policemen and reserve policemen who were ethnic Muslims in preparation of establishing a Muslim MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did this happen months before the outbreak of the war and months before the agreement on the transformation of the MUP into two MUPs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you about a crisis that broke out around the 20th of March. Is it correct that in co-operation -- or actually, that Alic, in co-operation with the chief of the station, carried out a fake police exercise involving the active-duty police and reserve police; and during this fake exercise he captured the arms depot and that that was quite drastic, but a conflict was avoided because the Serb side did not react?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that at the time because of such actions even two months before the war broke out many Serbs did not dare sleep in Zvornik; rather, they went to Karakaj or Mali Zvornik across the Drina River? Mali Zvornik is in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that this man, Alic, co-operated with the well-known Captain Hajro who was an active-duty military man deserted from the JNA in mid-1991 and worked on the establishment of the Patriotic League in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are we talking about Hajrudin Mesic, who after being killed his unit that attacked Zvornik often from Teocak was renamed the Hajrudin Mesic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Mr. Alic successful in infiltrating members of the Patriotic League into the MUP reserve force of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that he provided weapons for them, and in such an illegal manner created the core of the future Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in that way the reserve police force was infiltrated by well-known criminals and that they instilled fear in the rest of the policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of the fact that the party, the government, and all other institutions were either joint, in fact, or were sharing the same premises, is it true that you had learned that the Muslim side was involved in the preparation of plans for a possible blowing up of the Crveni Mulj dam in Zvornik which was actually a hazardous waste from the Glinica factory and would have contaminated all of the Serbian areas downstream and it would even harm Serbia in the process?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember knowing anything about plans to have the hydroelectric power-plant in Zvornik to be blown up as well as the bridges on the Drina and that those were the plans devised by the Patriotic League well before the outbreak of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember a crisis involving the dam in Visegrad, which is upstream of Zvornik some 50 or 60 kilometres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was common knowledge because there was live broadcasts on TV of that crisis as it unfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Murat Sabanovic, also another notorious criminal who later became the star of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, had prepared explosive for the purpose of blowing up the dam in Visegrad, that this was broadcast on television, and that Alija Izetbegovic and General Kukanjac communicated with him live on TV, on which occasion Alija Izetbegovic told him, "Don't do it for the time being." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everybody in Bosnia knows about this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you understand this as part of the overall plan of destroying the bridges and dams from Gorazde to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the idea was to cut us off from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that - and you mentioned that in examination-in-chief - that the Muslim side was arming themselves, that the weapons was brought in a variety of ways from Vienna, Croatia, up to Bosanski Brod, and that the Patriotic League and the SDA distributed these weapons either free of charge or through sale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that a certain number of Muslims from Zvornik were volunteers in the Croatian forces during the war between the JNA and Croatia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the SDA used to send people who were not policemen to attend certain courses, alleged courses, in Croatia and that quite a few of them were sent from Zvornik to attend these courses in 1991 in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a possibility for such training in Bosnia at the time and was it really necessary -- first of all, was there a proper school for the police officers in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Don't you find it a little bit odd for a political party to send people to attend police courses for people who are not members of the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 26th of July, 1991, in the youth library at Kula Grad, a branch of the Patriotic League was set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that eight months before the outbreak of war a unit was formed close to the very centre of Zvornik municipality and that the Serbs didn't have any problem in finding out about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: May I ask, Mr. Witness, how did you come to know that the Patriotic League was set up in 1991 in the youth library at Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look, we had offices, I mean SDA and SDS, it was a big office that was divided by a partition wall. We listened to each other. They listened to what we were talking about and we listened to them. And one of their members later wrote a book about their defence movement in Zvornik and he confirmed these dates in that book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you obtain a video-tape showing the formation of a branch of the Patriotic League in Godus village, which is your neighbouring village in Zvornik municipality, and is that the unit that you mentioned as being very well equipped which was intimidating in terms of the equipment that they had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you say that this unit was equipped close to standard of the NATO, did you say that in examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that was in October 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And there is a monument to this date standing at the location which testifies to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the Patriotic League and their Main Board issued a directive for the defence of the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina and instructions to that effect and that the leadership and the political and military staff of the Patriotic League was made up by the highest-ranking officials of the Muslims' part of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a little patience. I would like to show a document to the witness that displays and describes the activities and plans of the Patriotic League and the composition of the staff. We'll get back to this as soon as we find this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this: Was it crystal clear, not only to officials in the Serbian part of the government but also to ordinary people as well, that right before their eyes a powerful and elaborate network of the Patriotic League was in the process of being developed with units positioned in every village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are going to show a document about that as well, but let me ask you this: How did the Serbian people react to this information and to these preparations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the experience from history and since we were a minority, our reaction was fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who could have been this assumed, supposed enemy that this organisation was to target?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the Patriotic League was concerned, the target were the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that when the SDA was being founded on the 26th of May, 1990, a high-ranking official of Croatia and the Croatian Democratic Community said that Croatia was going to defend itself on the Drina, and was the Drina the boundary of the Independent State of Croatia during World War II?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember him saying that the border was going to be on the Drina, and that made us fearful because that coincided with the Independent State of Croatia, which had been fully supported by the Muslims. And we fared very badly in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll go back to this process of military organisation, but for now let me just establish a few things regarding the paper called or the papers called Variants A and B. In -- on page 82 of yesterday's transcript you spoke about this. Do you agree that in the title it is said how the Serbian people should behave under extraordinary circumstances rather than the SDS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that is how we understood it on the Crisis Staff because the Crisis Staff had members from Ante Markovic's party, from the League of Communists, et cetera. So we didn't see this as a partisan paper, but rather, a paper that would direct the behaviour of the Serbian people in a difficult situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that it did not reach you through ordinary party mail delivery. You are an educated man, you know how documents look like, but let me ask you this: In your view did this paper resemble more a kind of a general outline that has to be elaborated further rather than an adopted document? Because it didn't have any protocol number on the front page, that the signature says the "Crisis Staff," which was non-existent, and that there was no signature or stamp. When we speak about regular party documents, did they have a protocol number --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please pause before starting an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry, you started a bit too early. We didn't have the full translation of the last part of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do I have to repeat my question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Did they have a protocol number and then -- start from there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is: Was it customary practice for party papers that are finalised and adopted and accepted has protocol number in its heading, a date, and at the end of it it has a signature and a stamp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was customary procedure. We had a protocol book in which we registered such documents. We a secretary of our party, and we did not register it as a party paper because it did not arrive through the usual channels and by following the standard procedure when it concerned the party mail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder whether you answered the question in relation to whether this paper resembled more a kind of general outline than an adopted document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the best translation would be a draft. I don't know what the witness says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is clear that this is not an official document of any kind, judging by its contents, the missing stamp and the protocol number. So it's not a standard document but rather something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that nobody from the party headquarters ever called or sent anyone in order to monitor the implementation of the plan contained in that paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your previous statements as well as yesterday in examination-in-chief you confirmed that this paper, in your opinion, was exclusively for defence purposes, that you saw nothing negative in it, and that particularly Variant B was aimed at providing the protection of people, women, pregnant women, population in general?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that at this big meeting attended by 5- to 600 people nobody either discussed or voted on this paper, but that it was rather distributed as a kind of flyer without any adoption thereof and discussion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of the wording and the language used by the Main Staff, the Crisis Staff, and their advocating of support for the JNA, and in view of the wording of that very paper, does it appear to you reasonable that that paper came from well-meaning retired officers, army officers, who recommended that people should conduct themselves in this way if there should be a war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's one possible variant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you this: Do you agree with me that the goal, the objective, of the Muslim side was to subjugate the entire territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and put them under their own control and that the goal of the Serbian party was actually adapting, beginning from the maximum -- maximalist goal which would have been that Bosnia-Herzegovina should be part of Serbia and that that was not the plan of the Serbian Democratic Party, but that would have been the maximalist option for a portion of the population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's true. That was never an option of the Main -- of the headquarters of the party. It was just the wish of some of the individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree that it was optimal that the -- what the Serbian Democratic Party was advocating, which was a Yugoslavia of six republics, was actually an optimum solution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the next concession of the Serb side was to try and maintain a Yugoslavia consisting of four republics?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that once it became clear that the Muslim and the Croatian side would proceed with their secession plans, our next objective was to have the Serbian lands within Yugoslavia as one country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Maybe you're not aware of it, but this idea actually came from Mr. Izetbegovic. Did you know that Mr. Izetbegovic proposed to me that the Serb lands should remain within Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only indirectly. I read it in the papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was our next concession the one where we accepted that Bosnia and Herzegovina could be outside of Yugoslavia, provided that we had our own constituent unit within Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that our basic concern was that we should not be over-voted by a majority, that we should not be made poorer, and was it already your experience before the war - and you mentioned this yesterday when you talked about Zvornik - where the budgets were used and actually taken advantage of at the expense of the Serb people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that our concept was that this -- these would not be borders, but rather, that there would be an administrative reorganisation of municipalities. Thus, in Zvornik, for instance, there would be two municipalities, and Serb lands and Serb parts of the town and Serb quarters would be a Serb -- would constitute a Serb municipality, whereas the Muslim areas, Muslim parts of the municipality would constitute a Muslim municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there any negotiations on the way in that respect and would they have been successful had war not broken out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were negotiations going on and we even discussed details. However, when war broke out and -- all of that fell through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday that long before the war a Serb policeman did not dare go on assignment, venture into a Muslim area, if they had an assignment there, and that the same was true of Muslim policemen not daring to venture into Serbian areas. Was that one of the reasons why the police station had to be transformed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did all this contribute to the establishment of the Serbian municipality in Zvornik, and is it true that in the beginning this was just declarative and it was not actually put in place in real life? There was no official authority in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was only a declaration. We had no premises, no offices, nothing of that sort, but this was an attempt to exert political pressure on the Muslim authorities that were in the majority in order to get some gains for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned that Zvornik had been up until the 1960s a majority-Serb area, but then there was a change in the ethnic make-up of the municipality. And we heard today that the similar situation prevailed in Bratunac. But can you tell us now whether this was the result of a natural birth-rate, increase in the birth-rate, or whether it was affected by settlement, deliberate settlement, of the ethnic groups there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, it was a combination of both, natural birth-rate and also a planned migration to the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you mentioned - and you also stated so earlier in your statements - that a municipality was a state within a state. Was that an uncommon occurrence or was that in keeping with Tito's doctrine of an armed populace and in keeping with the Law on All People's Defence, where the municipality had a major role to play and the president of the municipality was also the president of the defence council of the municipality? And were you familiar with this administrative system of the former Yugoslavia and the Law on All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did say that it was a state within a state in view of two facts. First of all, because it was a territorial principle where the territory was considered a territory of an armed populace, and also because we were completely cut off from other Serb areas. There were no connections whatsoever between Zvornik and Pale and other areas. They were all -- we were practically completely isolated. We had no connections with them, and also following the principle of a self-organised government we organised ourselves. And as we could see yesterday, we even organised a way of funding our pensioners and finding funds for salaries and pays.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that among the documents of the municipal authorities, the provisional municipal authorities, there were also documents, appointments of judges and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the second half of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So was this the result of the inability to communicate with the centre of the Serbian authorities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the documents adopted by the provisional government and which were published in the bulletin of the Zvornik municipality, there are a number of appointments of judges, which is an eminently state function, which -- because the municipal -- the Assembly was unable to meet was vested in me up until the end of the summer 1992 and only after the summer of 1992 it was within the competence of the Assembly. So is that what you did in Zvornik municipality, because it was impossible for the state to appoint judges, that the municipality itself took it upon itself to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall that the provisional government in Zvornik appointed a misdemeanours judge and even a prosecutor for the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this was only the case up until the end of 1992, but it did not occur later, after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After that it was done by the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to dwell a bit on the following. You actually proclaimed a municipality, but it did not become operational until April, what, 5 or 6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's correct. We actually broke away from the municipality and then we tried to establish the offices, the police, the various government functions, the police, the judicial functioning, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that in the fax that you received in late March or early April, Momcilo Mandic informed you that the division within the MUP was agreed and the restructuring of the MUP was agreed and he referred to the Cutileiro Plan and the Izetbegovic-Karadzic agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. And it was also reported in the regular news that there was an agreement reached in Portugal, and that as a result, the then-minister of the interior, the -- Momcilo Mandic sent this telegram, where it was agreed that there would be a separation within the MUP and that there would be a Serbian MUP established but people could also choose to remain within the Muslim MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So it was not mandatory. It was left to the free will of individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. The principle of voluntary option was stressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were these negotiations on the transformation of the MUP conducted in good faith, were they carried out in a positive atmosphere, and was it envisaged that the equipment would be divvied up and did this happen before the conflict and did it suggest that this would have a positive outcome?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard this from the first time from Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and he said then that we would try and follow this. We would ask people to actually opt for whatever options they preferred. We agreed on the division of the material assets and everything else, premises, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the name of the gentleman -- the man who told that to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was Mr. Osman Mustafic, who was the chief of the police station in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, then, that in that case the Muslim MUP too would actually try to maintain law and order in Muslim areas, whereas the Serb MUP would take care of law and order in the Serb areas? And did this -- did the situation deteriorate when Muslim paramilitaries arrived in Serb areas and vice versa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was precisely the intention of this whole agreement, to actually bring some order, to disarm the village guards, because it was hard to work for the police in view of all the weapons that were actually were -- had been distributed to both parties, to either side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The false exercise where there was an attempt to capture the public security station around the 20th of March, which was conducted by Asim Alic, did he also use for this operation the reservists, some of whom had been criminals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, he did. He used reservists and also some other individuals who were not members -- active-duty police members. And they managed on that day or perhaps a day or two later or earlier to take control of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to shed some light on an incident where a number of extremists, criminals, were issued uniforms and long-barrelled weapons and they actually conducted patrols across the bridges before the war. Now, how did this arming of criminals -- what kind of effect did it have on Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometime before the war the reserve force which was actually strengthened by accepting new members and they did not -- they even accepted some criminals who had been convicted convicts, convicted of serious crimes including murder and so on, and when they were issued uniforms and long-barrelled weapons and automatic weapons and when this became something -- a well-known fact among the citizens in Zvornik, where Zvornik was practically an ethnically cleansed town of Serbs, there were only Muslims there, there was only one street where Serbs lived, well, that had a very negative effect. In the meantime, all of these policemen had also broken into their apartments and taken away their properties and their items from the apartments, and this only increased the tensions in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that happened before the outbreak of the conflict; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a few days before the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you confirmed during the examination-in-chief that for all of two months many Serbs would not spend the night in Zvornik. Just before the conflict broke out, all the Serbs, practically all the Serbs, went out either to Karakaj or to Serbia. Was that some kind of propaganda on our part or was this spontaneous? Could anybody have talked the Serbs into doing that or were they persuaded to do so by fear, authentic fear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, it was fear for life and children and families.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You did not get part of the station when the split took place, you had to move elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the rest of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only took our personal weapons and then we took two or three cars. And all the rest, including telecommunications equipment and most importantly the weapons that were there, 400 long-barrelled weapons I think, the Muslims kept all of that, along with accompanying equipment, such as ammunition and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, the interpreters didn't catch the first part of your answer, before you say: "We only took our personal weapons ..." Could you repeat the first part of your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this was the essence. We just took our personal weapons. We managed to get only the telecommunications equipment that we had on ourselves and we managed to get two or three cars. And what was the most important thing was the arms depot and they kept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please bear in mind, too, that it is important to put a pause between the question and answer. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the Muslim-Croat Rump Presidency, against the will of Mrs. Plavsic and Professor Koljevic and Professor Plavsic, on the 4th of April, on the day of Ramadan, the end of the Ramadan fast, declared general mobilisation of the Territorial Defence and the reserve police in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How could that have been understood? Who was the enemy apparent? The JNA had not been declared the enemy yet, so were we, the Bosnian Serbs, the only presumed enemy left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that Branko Grujic on the 5th of April declared a test mobilisation and on the 8th of April a true mobilisation in the Serb municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this preceded by a declaration of general mobilisation throughout Bosnia and also was it preceded by the killing of NCOs and soldiers in Sapna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Grujic's move was just a response, the only possible one, to the mobilisation that they carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, yesterday you said that at party level there was some kind of enhanced duty service on the part of the SDA and the SDS and the party Crisis Staff could only send reports and did not have any authority to act; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that only in the beginning of April, when this conflict broke out, a municipal Crisis Staff was established as a substitute for proper municipal government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that you left the Crisis Staff because you were disappointed because you had not been elected to a particular position that you had held. Was this an automatic thing after all, and during those few days were you on the Crisis Staff ex officio not by way of some kind of election or not as a consequence of your own choice or a choice having been made by somebody else? If you need to move into private session for this, tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was ex officio, ex officio I was a member of the Crisis Staff because I held that particular position. When I no longer held that particular position, I was no longer a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is what I'm interested in now: Let us identify what the initial positions of the Serb organs of government were in Zvornik, and we are going to see whether that was in line with the political positions of Serbs in Bosnia as a whole. You mentioned that the Serb side wanted to have a renowned cardiologist, a Muslim, Dr. Muhamed Jelkic, stay on as a member of the Serb Crisis Staff and in a way he was a member of the Muslim Crisis Staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I said yesterday was that -- I mean, well, it was the wish of the Serb Crisis Staff that Muhamed Jelkic be a kind of link between the Serb and Muslim Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So was that in accordance with your view that there should be an accommodation of views in order to reach agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked about the position of the Muslims after the crisis broke out. Is it correct that both in the police and in other organs and in various companies including your own, there were Muslims and those who worked received a salary as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the very beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that some lady by the name of Mirsada was appointed on the 1st of May to the Executive Board, or rather, the management board of Vitinka and that she's a Muslim too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D4035, could we have a look at that, please. Unfortunately, we have no translation. I kindly ask for your understanding because this is viva voce after all and we have to find our way as we move along.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a regular thing or actually is this a conclusion? It is the 21st of May and there is a number there and everything. Is this a conclusion stating that a provisional management board should be appointed for the company of Vitinka, the chairman of the board is Radenko Ristic, and members are Ljubo Jovic and Mirsada Mutapcic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just what is this exactly? Could I just know what the title is? I don't have a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Witness, do you know this rather than being unannounced of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an appointment of the provisional management board of the company of Vitinka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you can read it, but are -- whether you are in a position to testify to this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to admit that this is the first time that I see it as a document. Just like yesterday, I don't know what to say by way of comment. I can only read it, but -- actually, it's the first time I see the document, but I know that Ms. Mirsada was one of the top people in Vitinka. However, this is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask this: Do you know that there was no discrimination against Muslims at that time? This is May 1992. Is that in accordance with what happened where you were, people worked, received their salaries, and were also appointed to high management positions, although it was dangerous and difficult and unpleasant, but they were being appointed nevertheless?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, his evidence -- his answer will remain, but I don't see the point of admitting this document through this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D30 -- actually, 4034.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief you spoke about attempts to reach agreement and you talked about negotiations too. Did Mr. Izet Mehinagic take part in these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please zoom in. We have a translation too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have a look at this telegram. Is it correct that Mr. Izet Mehinagic is sending a telegram to General Savo Jankovic, commander of the Tuzla Corps of the JNA, and it is being CC'd to General Kukanjac? And I think we're going to see the date now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the bottom of this page, I think the date is the 5th -- no, it's the 8th, the 8th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us now -- I mean, we can all read it. Can you tell us what it says here, that Arkan was the main negotiator on the Serb side, that the Serb representatives were beaten up. Does this telegram confirm everything that you had described as a break in these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It also says that an offer was made to Zvornik to lay down their weapons and that the Crisis Staff of Zvornik decided on the ultimatum at 1600 hours and that his assessment was that the ultimatum would not be accepted and that there would be an unprecedented massacre of the unprotected innocent population. Is it correct that the Muslim part of the staff did not accept the terms for laying down weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Mr. Mehinagic says down here that Zvornik is a Yugoslav town and that the population is supposed to improve its attitude towards its own JNA and he says here this is only three days after the ambush and killing in Sapna; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go further down to see what the handwritten note is. No, actually, can we go up. Can we go up -- can we see the bottom -- or rather, the top of the page. We have it in English too actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "Colleagues please forward this telegram urgently, as urgently as possible ..." Oh, yes, that's typewritten. And it's handwritten that General Jankovic should be informed to take measures to protect --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Citizens in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Citizens in Zvornik and somebody from the command of the 2nd Military District signed this. You don't know whose signature this is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says so up here, Colonel Kecman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Colonel what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Kecman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Is it Kosovac maybe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but it's a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We can barely see. It may be Keserovic, but this is the essence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that this General Jankovic was forced to ask already on the 10th of April that action be taken against Kula Grad because they were firing at JNA soldiers on the right side, those who were guarding --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hydroelectric power-plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the bridges too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to call this up now, but can this telegram be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1605, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 00642 now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you noticed, but what we discussed, that dam, you see this terrible ecological catastrophe that is being envisaged in this letter because of these extremists or because of what they might do --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Muslim extremists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's also in accordance with your knowledge concerning plans to blow up dams; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crveni Mulj, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document dated the 10th of April. General Jankovic who did not like the SDS at all; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Savo Jankovic was a real communist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that he is asking that on the 10th that on the 11th action be taken against Kula Grad, and he says: "We are demanding action in order to neutralise the forces attacking our units which are defending the bridges on the Drina River."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that they did open fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a Croatian intercept because they were listening in to our conversations, and it says that the local authorities did not allow Arkan to liberate Kula Grad and that as a result he demonstratively left Zvornik. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally Arkan was ready to go and liberate Kula Grad immediately but he only had about 20 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Had they not fired from Kula Grad, would it have been ever liberated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so because that area is a purely Muslim populated part. However, it was impossible to live in Zvornik because it was exposed to constant fire coming from that direction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1606, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You took a position that self restraint by the Serbs with regard to Asim Alic's and his criminals' action in taking over the public security station was the one that prevented bloodshed. Is that your view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So a Crisis Staff was formed and it existed for a short period of time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was made up of personalities that were otherwise involved in some sort of government organs, and that was the basis on which they became members of the Crisis Staff not according to their political functions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned the president of the court, the misdemeanour judge, and other Serbs who held offices as a result of the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
