utterances.text: Is it correct - and if necessary, we may go into private session - is it correct that you stated that you had never attended a single meeting where there was any mention at all, let alone any debate, about burning houses and forcing people to leave their homes? We also mentioned mosques. Was it the government authorities that burned the mosques, did they encourage that, and did they know who did it overnight? (redacted) there was no debate about the destruction of any religious facility, about any burning of houses or dislocation of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also spoke earlier about the fact that you never attended a meeting where any mention was made of the need to kill the Muslims or to attack or cleanse the Muslim villages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say for certain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think we need a redaction, 62, 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go briefly into private session. I will state a reference and give my comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you still subscribe to the view that the JNA with time became predominantly Serb, among other things, due to the fact that the Muslims did not want to respond to call-ups to carry out their mandatory military service or to answer the call-up to join the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 4th or the 5th - and you mentioned that in examination-in-chief - a non-commissioned officer was killed and a number of soldiers were captured in Sapna. Was this unit advancing in a combat disposition or was it just moving towards Yugoslavia on the retreat from the Tuzla region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were just passing through Sapna, they were carrying out their regular task, and they were just marching through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that you mentioned that Semsudin Memovic [phoen] or Muminovic, a career officer who commanded some 17- or 18.000 men, a JNA unit made up of that number of men, deserted only on the 3rd of April and joined Hajrudin Mesic and the other deserters who had deserted much earlier, i.e., in mid-1991, and he took part in forming the units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the effect on the Serbs of the killing of this peaceful JNA column passing through Sapna without any combat deployment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that triggered the action and this was the last straw which was conducive to any failure to control the situation. All of the refusal by the Muslims to respond to call-up, the recognition of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the division of police stations, but this triggered actually -- this incident triggered the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if it is convenient, we will take a break now for half an hour and resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you, Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us dwell on these negotiations, Mr. Witness, for some time longer. Your view was, and you said that there was a video-tape, and you said that you wanted to reach an agreement with the Muslims to avoid anyone making any foolish move and that you wanted to await a solution for the entire Bosnia and Herzegovina. Was that position of the local leadership consistent with the position of the Serbian people in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at how these negotiations were terminated and can we see 65 ter 40011. This is a transcript of a video interview given by Mr. Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan, in which he describes the events and it more or less coincides with your description. So 65 ter 40011.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have been advised that it hasn't been released yet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We perhaps can leave it for later or for tomorrow, but I think it has been released.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm informed by Mr. Reid that it will take a few minutes for us to do whatever needs to be done with that. If there's another question that can be asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, apart from the Patriotic League, is it true to say that the Muslims had other notorious paramilitary groups in Zvornik, such as Dzamija Pigeons, Cobras, Black Swans, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you acquainted with the leaderships of these paramilitary groups? Did people know them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have a look at 1D40011 [as interpreted]. 1D4011, it's IIIA annex to report 674 of the Secretary-General from 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at this, this is annex III.A, S1994/674. S stands for report of the Secretary-General. Can we now look at page 11 of this document. Can you see here that it reads the Muslims and Croats -- the Mosque Doves and Pigeons in Zvornik and the United Nations are citing the sources from which they acquired this information and it says that they were using rifles from Hungary and Arabic countries. Both you and the rest of the people were aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There are other municipalities mentioned as well. This is a very useful document that we are going to refer to quite often at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You said this is a report of the Secretary-General?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This marking S1994/674, annex III.A, usually indicates an official document of the United Nations, or rather, the ones produced by the Secretary-General. We can look at the heading of the document if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The first page of this document says its source is "Submission of Permanent Mission of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to the Commission of Experts." So probably --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I couldn't find this, but I see that it was circulated as an official UN document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, probably, as you report, annexed this document. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Your Honours. I can't see the front page other than what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we upload the first page of this document, the bottom part. No, no, the up -- sources, yes, there. But you should have entire document of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it is a rather lengthy document. This is only a reference to the other identified groups, whereas there is also information on other paramilitary groups as well. If you don't mind, I would like to tender it. There are sources mentioned here, but this is a UN document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just that, Your Honour, the sources as far as I can see are a report titled "A New Genocide Against Serbs in Konjic Area" by the Association of Serbs from BiH, a letter, and Tanjug news sources. So I'll leave it with the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Separate from the issue of weight, how much weight it should be given, but I don't think there's any issue as to its authenticity. So as such, we can admit it. We'll give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1607, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may add, there is also a letter of the Croatian representative mentioned as a source.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, sir, was there also a group called the Cobras which, unlike the Mosque Doves which were in Konjic, were in Sapna or somewhere else? Was there a group named -- called the Cobras?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 1D3406.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 4036.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately we don't have a translation of this document. This is a document from the Croatian SIS, which is the Security and Information Service of the Bosnian Croats from 1996, an official note. If you take a look at this there is mention here of special-purpose units called the Black Swans. Did you know of the Black Swans?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please now read the official date. I believe that's the seventh line from the bottom, the official date when this group was established and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official date when this unit was established was the 31st of March, 1992. On that day on orders from Vahid Karavelic and the said Captain Labud, Hase Tiric, the current commander of the Black Swans, together with another 15 members of the Patriotic League went to Bijeljina with a task of establishing a special-purpose unit, and allegedly, at the time they engaged VRS in -- with the intention of taking control of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now could I just remind you that on the 31st of March, 1992, the VRS was not in existence as yet. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Arkan arrived in Bijeljina on the 1st of April, some 10 or so hours after the crisis erupted in Bijeljina, that's a generally known fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From this document from Croatian sources, can we clearly see that Vahid Karavelic sent Captain Labud and this other person, Hase Tiric and some other 15 members from the Patriotic League on the 31st of March to Bijeljina and that they provoked the crisis, and Arkan only arrived after the crisis erupted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a well-known fact that Bijeljina was first taken over by Muslims and that only later it was taken over by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having heard the witness's answer, do we need to admit this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I believe it could assist the Trial Chamber with the context, and this is to show how the Croatian side had information that this unit was established on the 31st and that 15 men had been sent to Bijeljina on the 31st. We saw here -- we heard evidence that the crisis in Bijeljina erupted on the 31st of March, in the evening, and that it actually flared up on the next day, on the 1st of April, after Arkan arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm just trying to see again what the date of this document is which I can't see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the top of the page we see the date, the 9th of May, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, that with the answers given, I don't see this document from that much time later assisting, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And given the position that the witness would not be in a position to comment on this document himself. I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1608, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Witness, that all these units from the Patriotic League, then the Territorial Defence, the Green Berets, the Cobras, the Mosque Doves and so on, later became part of the BH army, although some of them still retained their old names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now take a look at 1D4037, please. We don't have a translation of this document either, unfortunately, but I will make an introduction. This is from Bosnia and Herzegovina, a document compiled on the 25th of August, 1997. The ministry of -- the Croatian Defence Council, and it says additional information on the engagement of Dzemal Merdan, and so on and so forth. Could we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to refer you to the bottom of the second paragraph: "In early 1991 ..." Could you please read out that sentence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In early 1991, in those towns where Muslims had an absolute majority, small armed units local in character were established. "As they were not linked up in their operations, the leadership of the SDA in the course of March 1991 entrusted a number of its members, Munib Bisic; the current brigadier general of the BH army, the chief of the military mission of the BH federation, Hasan Cengic; Hasan Efendic, and so on, that they out of the officer corps of the then-JNA, or rather, of the Muslim -- of members of the Muslim ethnicity who had left JNA units or intend to leave them, should form the corps which would take care of military issues. "A headquarters which was established in August was made up of Sulejman Vranj, Rifat Bilajac, Meho Karisik, Sefer Halilovic, Atif Saronjic, Mustafa Hajrulahovic, Feid Heco, Dervo Harbinja, Salko Polimac, Alija Loncaric, Hajrudin Suman, Zijo Rasidagic, Zaim Backovic, Kerim Lucarevic, and Hasan Cengic. The commander of the staff was Meho Karisik, the current BA general -- BH Army general."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is in March 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The information that the Croats had on Bosnia, was it something that was known by us as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you know what this document is about? It's dated 1997, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I -- this is a -- what I said was that I knew about the leadership and the leaders they appointed. I don't know anything about the document itself, but I know these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go -- sorry, Your Honour, could we go into private session for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 40011, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Reid tells me that 4011A may be the correct document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a transcript of a TV interview. Here it says the president -- or in other words, he is being interviewed in his capacity as the president of the Party of Serb Unity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, while we wait for this to come up, sir, let me ask you this: Do you know that this party and Arkan himself were investigated by OSCE and that he was permitted to take part in the elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I am aware of the participation of this party in the election in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And his -- he received some funds from the OSCE for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, as every other party, his party too received some funds for the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And his group of some 15 or so members of parliament entered the parliament, right, his party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, he also had his assemblymen in the Serbian parliament.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is not the document that I had in mind. The English version is ET V000-1946. [In English] And again, 1946. Transcript, English translation V000-1946.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This bears the same number. Go up.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: But I have it completely different graphically. It is with numbers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have the time-frame for that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: 620. 00.00.00-00.06.20. [Interpretation] 1430, so we should go back to 620.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It will take a couple minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then I'll deal with something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we not have the video itself?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We haven't prepared it. We thought this was faster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you have some other question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, by all means, I'll deal with something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you said here that after this arming took place and organisation of the Patriotic League in Kula already in July 1991, you said that the Serb side was in a situation to ask for something as well, and you described going to Radmilo Bogdanovic. When was that, what month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So for at least six months you hadn't done anything in that respect; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said yesterday that Grujic did something very minor before that, say in November 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please look at one intercept where somebody is calling me from Zvornik, and that is 65 ter 31757. Please have the English version as well. Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the end of August 1991. Do you remember that until the end of August 1991 there was hope that the historic Serb-Muslim agreement would be reinforced, the one that Zulfikarpasic and I worked on with the initial support of Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that at the end of July we were in Zvornik - let us not mention the position you had then in Zvornik - and do you remember that we had this big rally of Serbs and Muslims at the end of July 1991, Mr. Zulfikarpasic and I, and that the hall was chock-a-block full of Serbs and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that Izetbegovic purportedly still supported that document, but there was this group of SDA extremists that was shouting against the agreement and against Zulfikarpasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that already then things were getting out of control and that although there was police protection for the safety of Mr. Zulfikarpasic, we did not dare go to have dinner at Vidikovac, so we got out through Karakaj, Caparde, Sekovici, Serb-held areas, to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that towards the end of August Mr. Izetbegovic withdrew his agreement to that agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So please let us have a look at this. Somebody is asking to speak to me, some Bogicevic from Zvornik. Can we now have the next page, please. I either was not there or I could not answer the phone. And finally when I hear what that was all about, I do answer the phone. So he is saying that some weapons are being distributed, and this is the first time that Karadzic shows up here. Do you see here towards the top of the Serbian page it says: "Zulfikarpasic and Karadzic were here in Zvornik and they had problems and I don't know what, TV Belgrade," and so on and so forth. Is he speaking about these problems with these SDA extremists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's around the middle in the English version. Let me just have a look at this for a moment, please. He says -- right. He says that some weapons are being distributed and this secretary of mine is probably saying: "Who distributed it, Karadzic?" And Bogicevic says: "No, not Karadzic." And this man says: "Then who was it?" And he says: "Brane Grujic distributed it." And then: "Ah-ha," Bogicevic says, "SDS Zvornik president." And this other one says: "Listen, I cannot believe that." And can we have the next page now, please. Obviously the situation was such that I had to answer the phone and you see that I did answer the phone. Isn't that right? Now he's asking me whether I know Brano Vujic or Grujic and I say I don't. And he says, well, he's the president of the SDS. And I say I cannot know every president and I cannot believe that weapons are being distributed. Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't know what the witness testified to in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, it was only then, that is to say, the end of August, somebody was dealing with that. The witness thinks that it's November actually, and the witness himself went to see Bogdanovic only in the beginning of 1991, and that before this, the Muslim side had already set up its entire organisation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, it was the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were there in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Muslims started organising themselves in March 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, do you know who this Mr. Bogicevic is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know Milorad Bogicevic in Zvornik. To the best of my knowledge, no such person exists there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And do you know who Brane Vujic is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably they mean Brano Grujic, so Grujic, Vujic. Brano Grujic was president of the municipal board of the SDS. As for Vujic, I think that's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any observation, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have no objection to it being admitted, Your Honour. You will also see on the bottom of the second page in the English they do use the name as Brano Grujic as the person distributing weapons. So I think it does tie-in to the topics the witness has discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1610, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, the number, I think, for the clip we were looking for is 40011B.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 6 minutes, 20 seconds probably. Right? Can we have that now? There is a Serbian version too. Can we ask for the Serbian version to be on half of the screen for the witness's benefit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm afraid we don't have B/C/S version, so that's why I asked whether you -- we have clip -- the video itself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I'd like to read it out, with your leave. This is what he says from line 22. He's actually -- actually, from line 13 he is saying that in Erdut he was informed that Serbs were being slaughtered in Bijeljina, that extremist Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. Mr. Reid tells me he thinks he can play the audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's more convenient. We can follow with this transcript and the witness can follow the video clip itself. Is there a way in which the interpreters could follow this transcript while watching the video?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can give them the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We could have the transcript printed and distributed that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the transcript to be distributed, shall we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And are we ready? One further delivery. I think we are now ready to view the video. Can you play the video?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 6.20, please. We don't need all of this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Commander of the Serb Volunteer Guard. "God help you, brothers and sisters. I would also like to greet these wonderful children because they are our future. We live for the sake of our children" --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is an election rally. Can we view it from 6.20. We don't need to see all of it. If we get more time, I don't mind watching all of it, but I'm afraid that I'll be wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, we may need to see the hard copy of the transcript. Mr. Reid has printed the part up to 6.20, he thought that was what was being asked for. This is the part we've got in the B/C/S as well. I'm not sure he knows exactly -- we need to see exactly which text is requested because I think what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's in the e-court. With your personal computer you can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My understanding is what's in e-court goes from 0 to 6.20, which is what has been printed and what is on the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So if it's from 6.20 later, then that means, as far as I can understand, we don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, the transcript says it's from the beginning until 6.20.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Well, then let's play it, but it seems to me that -- well, actually, it's more of an interview than a presentation, but okay, let's have it played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we start from the beginning. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "President of the Serbian Unity Party and commander of the Serbian Volunteer Guard. "God help you, brothers and sisters. I would like also to greet these wonderful children because they are our future. We live for the sake of our children. I would like to tell you that my wife Ceca wanted to come with me, but since she is six months pregnant I did not allow it. She sends her regards to all of you. "Brothers and sisters, you know that from the very first day, the Serbian Volunteer Guard has defended Serbian homeland, Serbian people, Serbian children, because by defending your children we were defending ours, because it would be our turn sooner or later. "And that is how it started and so we come to the moment when I was informed in Erdut that Serbian population was being slaughtered in Bijeljina, that extremist Muslim groups, certain Handzar divisions infiltrated Bijeljina, that genocide threatened Bijeljina. We immediately responded to this appeal, although we were supposed to go and defend Herzegovina. Straight away we redirected our convoy and entered Bijeljina during the night. We fought the whole day and kept Bijeljina. We defended the Serbian people. "Then an appeal came saying that Zvornik was Muslim. Two Serbs, former officials, are negotiating with two Muslims, one of them was a commander of Muslim army and the other president of the SDA. I cannot remember the names, because I lose my senses when it is them, I cannot remember the names. They negotiated in Mali Zvornik about the surrender of Karakaj where Serbs -- some Serbs fled. We came into that room in Mali Zvornik. I asked them who they were. He said he was a Serb, he was called that and that, representing that and that. They are your countrymen and I would not like to embarrass them here. The other one said the same. The other two -- one said, 'I am the President of the SDA' and the other said he was the would-be commander of their army. I asked the Serbs, 'What are you negotiating, who gave you the right to betray Zvornik and the Serbian people here?' And then we did not beat the Muslims, we beat the two Serbs because they betrayed all of you and Zvornik. "At 5.00 in the morning I ordered an attack on Zvornik and it was liberated, except for the tower up there, in record time. Two of my officers were killed there - Ivan Okiljevic, a.k.a., Rambo, a young man who fought on all battle-fields and who was the engine of the volunteer guard, along with Major Zika. Two fatalities, two officers in Zvornik, but with these losses and with that Serbian blood we marked this as a Serbian town. "Let us get one thing clear, the Serbian Volunteer Guard afterwards moved to other battle-fields. We organised Serbian control here, which has not been functioning well, Yellow and Green Wasps and Blue Wasps appeared - I do not know their names - they were behaving violently, so I had to put things in order once again when I was passing through Zvornik. I am saying this for the history, for the sake of truth, and those who participated in combat here know that it was like this. Zvornik was free, Serbian Volunteer Guard went to other battle-fields, and we set up the border on the Drina River. If we had not taken Zvornik and Bijeljina, take my word for it, the border would be here on the Drina now, and God knows how many victims there would be among the Serbian population."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think we can stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, is this an election rally, election rally, held in a hall in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge was there any hindrance by the OSCE or NATO, banning Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan, and his party to participate in the political life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they participated just like any other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this description that he gave, although it was a bit summarised and suited for a political rally, but is the essence consistent with what you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1611, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The date of this video is September 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's an election rally, but he's talking about the events from April 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 65 ter 40162 and I think we have an English version, too, in e-court. We are waiting for the Serbian version. This is a TV interview with Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan, from July and August 1994, production from July and August 1994. Can we have ERN page in the Serbian with the last three digits 395. I think that's page 8 and I believe that the same page is in English as well. The time is 1.16.35. Yes, we have it in English. 1.16.35.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the Serbian version. He's being asked here about his connections with the JNA and he says that he didn't have any contacts, that he didn't receive anything from them, that he was the sole source of financing the Serbian Volunteer Guard with which they procured weapons. He is talking about fighting in Croatia, Tenja, Ernestinovo, et cetera; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move two pages forward. Time-frame 1.24. Can we have the next page in the Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look here where he says in the then-Bosnia-Herzegovina the Muslims armed themselves, that there were over 300 Kalashnikovs in Janja, 600 Kalashnikovs in Bijeljina itself, and that a Croatian unit consisting of Albanians had already been inserted into Bijeljina and was supposed to assume power overnight in Bijeljina. This means that all prominent Serbs -- there was a list for the liquidation of all prominent Serbs who were supposed to be killed in the 24 hours. And then he goes on to describe this one day of fighting, and when the fighting ceased he describes the arrival of Mr. Abdic and Biljana Plavsic. Was Mr. Abdic the Muslim member of the Presidency, Biljana Plavsic the Serbian member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He says here that they used automatic rifles from Croatia, that there were four or five Serbs with their throat slit, they were experienced enough, and they speedily took it over. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have time-frame 1.29.39. Page 13 in English. We need page 12, I think, in Serbian. It says: "After that you consolidated power here in Bijeljina ... a little bit later Operation Zvornik commenced." And he said that he had received information that the Muslims had taken over Zvornik. Is it correct that before this action the Muslims had taken over Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That the Serbian authorities and the Serbian people fled across the river to Karakaj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to -- for you to look at the rest of this text, and it says here that he thought that the Serbs entered negotiations with a view to handing over Karakaj, which says that -- that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably next page for B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. It's a different sequence on the pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He says: "We are going to give them Karakaj ..." But in the previous document we thought that he believed that the Serbs were there to negotiate the hand-over of the Serbian part of Zvornik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the confusion was about. Our two representatives were only discussing the division and we decided to wait peacefully for the final solution for the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here he repeats what you already said, who gave you the right, you have no right, no mandate. He slapped them a couple of times on the face. We didn't touch the Turks. And he gave them a piece of paper and asked them to write down all the weapons that they had. They wrote that they had 700 armed people and how those people were deployed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please read all of this from -- until 1.33.38, because it says that eventually special units from Pale came and disarmed these paramilitary formations all around Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1612, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, let us now focus on the issue of paramilitary. Yesterday you were asked with the affirmative connotation in the question about whether the government financed paramilitary troops. Now my question is: Was the question of volunteers regulated by the law and by a separate decision of the SFRY Presidency, whereby the volunteers were completely put on equal footing with the soldiers from the regular army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct -- I'm waiting for the interpretation. Is it correct that the reservists who were employed were called up to take part in exercises and received salary for that period, whereas those who were unemployed, it was the army who paid them daily allowance during exercises?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct - and I think you confirmed this already somewhere - that not a single organised unit came to Zvornik with the exception of the Arkan's unit, which stayed there for a short period of time, and that all the rest came as volunteers in their civilian clothes and without weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that they were assigned to the Territorial Defence and later to the Army of Republika Srpska and that quite a large number of the volunteers remained on the lines and in the army and adhered to their obligations? On the other hand, some of them returned and became renegades of a certain period of time, that is to say, paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did any of them came as paramilitary in the first place or did they come individually as volunteers, whereas the paramilitary formations were later formed by those renegade elements and some local elements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I said that they came individually and these paramilitary formations were later formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm afraid that because of potential overlap, his answer to your previous question was not reflected in the transcript. Did you say "yes" to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I'd like to ask something before I show a particular document. Since this is a viva voce witness and since the OTP spent about five hours, could I perhaps have the rest of tomorrow except for the time that is required for re-direct, because it would really be a pity. This is a witness who took part in government before the war and who saw a great deal during the critical period of time. It would be a pity to see him leave without being fully examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The fact itself that the witness was changed into a viva voce witness does not necessarily mean that you will have more time, but we'll see tomorrow how much more you will need. And please be efficient as much as possible. I think it's time to rise for today. Do you have a further question to put -- yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would have one point I would like to make at the end for just a minute in private session if we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It can be in the presence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Probably better out of the presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. So that's it for today, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, I hope that I'm going to get five hours at least but I'm hoping for more because of the extent to which this witness is beneficial for the Trial Chamber because the Prosecution spent almost five hours with this witness. I've been allocated three and a half. I hope it's not going to remain that way, only three and a half. I would need all of tomorrow except for the time needed by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll deal with that matter first thing tomorrow. The witness can be excused. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, just a second. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Mr. Harvey, it will be a long day for you. We rise. Tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of August, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
